searchText: This option came up a lot in various forms during the ASE discussions and it was always shot down due to it decreasing collision resistance. It was assumed (with good reason IMO) that collision resistance was already too weak at 80-bits and decreasing it would just make the situation worse. If you want to pursue that, I think the number one hurdle is putting forward a strong convincing argument that we don't need address collision resistance. I could make a more detailed post on "what exactly would not having collision resistance break" I think it may also help to include specifics on how much collision resistance we think we'll need in ~5 years for the various things. It would be very interesting to read in more detail what type of corner cases would require collision resistance 🙂 I'm having trouble remembering what the problems were with extending to 32 bytes. My memory was that they weren't hard blockers.
